validity.recommendation: Keep Diameter blank on the Wild Trail Project row (and keep LengthKnownKm at 0.00) -- do not carry the gem.wiki system infobox figure of '24 in; 30 in' onto this project. Williams' own Wild Trail fact sheet states outright, under 'Construction Activities': 'The project includes a new compressor station, adjacent to the existing Northwest Pipeline Clay Basin Meter Station. No new pipelines are proposed in this project.' FERC's own Notice of Schedule (Docket CP25-497-000) independently describes the project as 'the construction of the proposed new Daggett Compressor Station' with no mention of new mainline pipe -- two independent publishers agree. The project's only piping is short 24-inch suction/discharge yard piping tying the new Daggett Compressor Station into Northwest's EXISTING 26-inch mainline (compressor-station yard piping, not new transmission length). No new mainline pipe is laid, so per the standing expansion rule the blank Diameter is correct and confirmed, not a gap.
validity.researcher_notes: Fetched Williams' 'Wild Trail Project' fact sheet PDF directly (williams.com) and read it with pdftotext -layout: 'Construction Activities: The project includes a new compressor station, adjacent to the existing Northwest Pipeline Clay Basin Meter Station. No new pipelines are proposed in this project. Scope of Work: Installing Taurus 70 Gas Turbine compressor.' Target in-service Q4 2027 (consistent with the sheet's existing StartYear1=2027, which was not flagged). Cross-checked against FERC's Notice of Schedule for the EA (90 FR 42760-42761, FR Doc 2025-16953, Docket CP25-497-000, 2025-09-04, read via the Federal Register raw-text API): 'Northwest proposes to add an additional 51,955 dekatherms per day ... through the construction of the proposed new Daggett Compressor Station (Daggett CS).' A separate web summary of the same docket's EA-availability notice additionally describes '24-inch-diameter suction and discharge yard piping to interconnect the Daggett Compressor Station to Northwest's existing 26-inch-diameter Northwest Pipeline' -- confirming the only piping involved is short compressor-station yard piping into an EXISTING 26-inch mainline, not new transmission pipe, and not the '24 in; 30 in' the wiki carries for the wider system. Both cited URLs verified OK via scripts/url_verifier.py.
